name: Niger
fact: The historic desert city of Agadez showcases an impressive earthen mosque featuring a 27-meter minaret, the tallest mud-brick structure of its kind.

name: Nigeria
fact: Celebrated worldwide as a creative powerhouse, Nigeria produces chart-topping Afrobeats music and an innovative film industry that inspires audiences across continents.

name: Rwanda
fact: Successful community-led conservation in Volcanoes National Park has helped Rwanda steadily increase its population of endangered mountain gorillas over recent decades.

name: São Tomé and Príncipe
fact: Renowned as the Chocolate Islands, this volcanic archipelago cultivates premium organic cocoa alongside lush rainforests protected within a designated UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.

name: Senegal
fact: Every winter, millions of migratory birds gather at the Djoudj National Bird Sanctuary, creating one of the world's most spectacular avian refuges.

name: Seychelles
fact: The remote Aldabra Atoll provides a pristine sanctuary for more than one hundred thousand giant tortoises, the largest wild colony on Earth.

name: Sierra Leone
fact: Nestled in the rainforest near Freetown, Tacugama Chimpanzee Sanctuary rescues vulnerable primates and leads vital conservation education initiatives throughout the country.

name: Somalia
fact: Treasured as a nation of poets, Somalia honors an illustrious oral storytelling tradition while bordering mainland Africa's longest coastline along the Indian Ocean.

name: South Africa
capital: Pretoria (executive; Cape Town legislative, Bloemfontein judicial)
fact: The Cape Floral Region forms one of Earth's richest botanical hotspots, sheltering thousands of endemic flowering plant species found nowhere else.

name: South Sudan
fact: Spanning across expansive savannahs and wetlands, the Great Nile Migration sees millions of antelopes traverse South Sudan in the largest land mammal migration on Earth.

name: Sudan
fact: The archaeological park of Meroë preserves more than two hundred steep-sided stone pyramids that showcase the remarkable architectural legacy of the ancient Kingdom of Kush.

name: Tanzania
fact: Rising majestically above the plains, Mount Kilimanjaro stands as Africa's highest mountain and the tallest free-standing volcanic peak in the world.

name: Togo
fact: The UNESCO-inscribed Koutammakou landscape features remarkable two-story mud tower-houses known as Takienta, reflecting ingenious traditional architecture and harmony with nature.

name: Tunisia
fact: The colossal third-century Amphitheatre of El Jem stands remarkably intact in central Tunisia as an exceptional masterpiece of ancient Roman monumental architecture.

name: Uganda
fact: The snow-capped Rwenzori Mountains, historically called the Mountains of the Moon, feature rare equatorial glaciers and dramatic afro-alpine vegetation along Uganda's western border.

name: Zambia
fact: Victoria Falls plunges into the Zambezi River gorge, generating a colossal curtain of falling water whose misty spray can be seen dozens of kilometers away.

name: Zimbabwe
fact: The magnificent granite ruins of Great Zimbabwe stand as a testament to medieval African architectural genius, featuring massive dry-stone walls built entirely without mortar.
